tldr: This survey-data page contains 30+ public comment submissions from business owners, non-profits, government officials, and individuals across Oregon. Dominant themes: CAT tax and regulatory burden discourage business; permitting processes overly complex; K-12 and higher education chronically underfunded; childcare system misaligned with working-family hours; sectoral constraints (marine industrial, agriculture, rural economies); and calls for economic development restructuring. Multiple respondents benchmark against Arizona, Texas, Florida, Idaho, Tennessee, and Washington as superior business climates.

bullets.text: CAT (Corporate Activity Tax) cited repeatedly by multiple respondents as major business burden; calls for elimination or reform
Permitting complexity highlighted as critical barrier—example: single wetlands issue requires 3 agency approvals instead of 1
K-12 education described as 'plummeted to one of the worst in the country'; calls for teacher wage tables and outcome-based funding
Higher education funding lowest in nation; University of Oregon reports $15 ROI per $1 invested but state support inadequate
Childcare system misaligned: state funds ~20,000 preschool children but programs operate 8:30-3:30 only; working families need 7am-6pm coverage
Marine industrial businesses constrained by regulations/permitting along Willamette; Portland EOA analysis undercounts available industrial land
Agricultural water parity requested: Oregon irrigates <1M acres from Columbia River vs. Washington/Idaho each irrigating 3M+ acres
Tourism sector (Oregon's 3rd largest industry) lacks state strategy representation; transient lodging tax diverted from intended use
Rural arts institutions generate $1.5M annual economic impact but face 30% ticket-sale decline due to lack of stable state funding
SB 1507 concern: federal tax conformity loss (QSBS, bonus depreciation elimination) raises capital cost for early-stage venture-backed companies
